entry.title: My German learning journey starts
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
I suppose it is time I got serious about learning German. I have spent more than a year in Berlin and haven't participated in any of the communities I wanted to come here for. A major mental hurdle is that I don't know German, and most of the chats/websites I can find are in German.

Or this is just another excuse to keep myself from going out of my apartment.

Regardless, Deutsch lernen is my priority #1 until I am fluent.

entry.title: The case system
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
• There are four German cases
    1. The Nominative Case - Der Nominativ
    2. The Accusative Case - Der Akkusativ
    3. The Dative Case - Der Dativ
    4. The Genitive Case
  • Personal pronouns also change with case
  • Word order in german
    • German allows freedom of word placement
    • Meaning of sentence is derived from the case rather than the word order
    • Examples
      • The man pets the dog
        • Der Mann streichelt den Hund
        • Den Hund streichelt der Mann
      • Is the man petting the dog?
        • Streichelt der Mann den Hund?
        • Streichelt den Hund der Mann?

  • Prepositions that can either be dative or accusative

    an at
    auf on
    hinter behind
    in in
    neben next to
    unter under
    über over, on top of, above
    vor in front of
    zwischen between
    • When they tell the position of something, corresponding word is in dative case
      • e.g Der Mann steht vor dem Eingang
    • When they tell the motion of something, corresponding word is in accusative case
      • e.g Der Mann läuft vor den Eingang

entry.title: The Genitive Case
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
The des der des der
A eines einer eines  
  • Used to express possession
    • In English possession is shows with an apostrophe + s e.g the girl's ball
  • Answers whose? (wessen?)
  • Used most often in written German
    • In spoken German, von (from) and the dative case is used instead
  • Masculine and neuter forms require either an -s or es ending
    • Single syllable words take an es ending
    • Multiple syllables take an -s ending
    • Examples
      • Der Koffer des Mannes (The man's suitcase)
      • Die Spielzeuge des Kindes (The child's toys)
      • Das Buch meines Bruders (My brother's book)
      • Das Auto meiner Schwester (My sister's car)
  • Examples
    • My father's house
      • Das Haus meines Vaters (Genitive case)
      • Das Haus von meinen Vater (Dative case)
  • Prepositions that take genitive case
    • anstatt (instead of)
    • außerhalb (outside of)
    • innerhalb (inside of)
    • trotz (despite)
    • während (during)
    • wegen (because of)

entry.title: The Dative Case - Der Dativ
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
The dem der dem den
A einem einer einem  
English Nominative Dative
I ich mir
you(s) du dir
he er ihm
she sie ihr
it es ihm
we wir uns
you(pl) ihr euch
they sie ihnen
  • Describes the indirect object of a sentence
  • Answers the question to who? (wem?) or what? (was?)
  • Used for indirect objects which usually receive an action from the direct objects (in the accusative case)
  • Examples
    • I am giving you a flower
      • Ich schenke dir eine Blume
      • Eine Blume schenke ich dir
    • Der Jungen gibt dem Mann den Schlüssel
      • Subject (who or what is giving) : Der Jungen
      • Direct object (who or what is given): den Schlüssel
      • Indirect object (to who or to what is given): dem Mann

  • Prepositions that take dative case

    aus from, out of
    außer besides, except
    bei at, near, next to
    gegenüber opposite
    mit with
    nach to, after
    seit since
    von of, from, about
    zu to

  • Some verbs always take the dative case

    Verb Meaning
    antworten to answer
    begegnen to meet
    gefallen to be pleasing, to like
    gehören to belong to (ownership)
    glauben to believe
    helfen to help
    nützen to use
    passen to fit
    passieren to happen
    schmecken to taste

entry.title: The Accusative Case - Der Akkusativ
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
The den die das die
A einen eine ein  
  • Answers the question whom? (wen?)
  • Describes the direct object of a sentence
  • Known as objective case in English
  • Only masculine articles change in the accusative case
  • Examples
    • Das kind isst einen Apfel
    • Der Mann liebt die Frau
    • Die Frau liebt den Mann
  • Some prepositions always take the accusative case
    • durch (through)
    • bis (until)
    • für (for)
    • ohne (without)
    • entlang (along)
    • gegen (against)
    • um (around)

entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
The der die das die
a ein eine ein  
  • It describe the subject of a sentence
  • It answers the question who? (wer?)
  • Examples
    • Die (Eine) Frau lebt in Deutschland
    • Der (Ein) Mann arbeitet in der Bäckerei
    • Das (Ein) Kind geht in die Schule

entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
• To ask questions, switch the position of subject and verb. e.g

    Statement Question
    Kanada ist groß Ist Kanada groß?

Die W-Wörter - The W-words

Word Meaning Example
Wer Who  
Wie How Wie geht's (How is it going)? Wie heißt du (How are you called)?
Woher Where from Woher kommst du (Where are you from)?

entry.title: Verbs
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
• Verbs when not in a sentence have an infinitive ending, ending in en
    • e.g kochen (to cook)
      • "koch" is called the stem/base of the verb
  • In German same verb form is used for things you do habitually and things you're doing right now
    • Examples
      • Ich singe oft (I often sing)
      • Ich singe jetzt (I am singing now)

  • Verbs have different endings depending on the subject of the sentence

    Subject Verb (schwimmen)
    ich schwimme
    du schwimmst
    er / sie schwimmt

  • Present tense verb endings

    Subject Ending
    ich e
    du st
    er/sie t
    wir en
    ihr t
    sie/Sie en

entry.title: Articles
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
• A grammar system that associates one of three genders with every noun
  • There is a separate article for every gender
Type Male Female Neutral English
Definite der die das The
Indefinite ein eine ein A/An
  • The case system adds a lot of variety to articles

    • Nominative: who is performing the action

      English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
      The der die das die
      a ein eine ein  

    • Accusative: on whom the actions is being performed

      English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
      The den die das die
      A einen eine ein  

    • Dative: with what the actions is being performed

      English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
      The dem der dem den
      A einem einer einem  

    • Genitive: expresses possession (only used in writing, in speaking dative is used)

      English Masculine Feminine Neuter Plural
      The des der des der
      A eines einer eines  

  • Some words can have different meaning based on which article is used with them. Example: band

    German English
    Der Band Volume (of a book)
    Die Band music band (group of musicians)
    Das Band Ribbon (hair band)

entry.title: Nouns - Die Nomen
entry.author: Charanjit Singh
entry.content:
• Nouns are people, places, things and ideas
  • When writing, nouns are always capitalized
  • Every noun has a gender and a corresponding article to show it

Duzen und siezen

  • Duzen means addressing someone with "du"
  • Siezen means addressing someone with "sie"
  • Don't use 'du' with someone unless they initiate it

Du kannst mich duzen (You can address me as "du")

Personal Pronouns

German English
ich I
du you
er he
sie she
es it
wir we
ihr you (pl)
sie they

Noun Plurals

Noun plurals are 4 to 9 distinct modifications made to nouns based on

  • how the noun is spelled
  • what gender the noun has
  • how many syllables
  • which syllable is being emphasized

Plural endings

  • -(e)n
    • Used by 90% feminine nouns
  • - (no change)
    • Used by family members e.g Vater, Mutter, Bruder, Schwester
    • Table settings e.g Teller, Gabel, Schüssel, Messer, Löffel
  • -s
  • -e
    • Used by 90% male nouns
    • Used by 75% neuter nouns
  • -<umlaut>e
  • -<umlaut>er
